authorization: https://nmap.org/book/legal-issues.html — scanme.nmap.org is explicitly provided by the Nmap Project for people to test scanning tooling against. Light, non-intrusive probing only.
scope: Hand-labeled ground truth for the active worker's SAFE modules only (http_probe, header_check, tls_inspect/grade, exposed_file). This is a SMALL, approximate reference set used to compute a crude false-positive rate; scanme's live configuration can drift, so treat the number as indicative, not authoritative.

classes.signal: A legitimate, correctly-reported observation we expect the scanner to surface for this host (true positive).
classes.noise: Informational / tool-availability output that is accurate but is NOT an actionable vulnerability; if it is ever escalated to >= low severity that is a false positive.
classes.false_positive_if_present: This host does NOT expose the resource/condition. If the scanner emits this finding at all, it is a false positive.

missing-content-security-policy.note: The default Apache page genuinely ships no CSP header.

missing-frame-protection.note: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is present.

missing-strict-transport-security.note: Only valid if probed over HTTPS; scanme is HTTP-only, so this should normally NOT appear. If it appears on an HTTP-only probe it is a false positive.

tool-unavailable-tlsx.note: tlsx binary not installed in this run environment; accurate availability notice, not a vulnerability.

tool-unavailable-nuclei.note: nuclei binary not installed; availability notice, not a vulnerability.

exposed-git-head.note: scanme does not serve a .git directory.

exposed-env.note: scanme does not serve a .env file.

exposed-env-local.note: scanme does not serve a .env.local file.

exposed-aws-credentials.note: No AWS credentials file is exposed.

exposed-config-backup.note: No PHP config backup is exposed.

exposed-apache-server-status.note: mod_status should not be world-readable here.

notes: Recall is measured only against expected_signal_rule_ids (the actionable, severity >= low findings we expect on a plain HTTP probe of scanme). Info-level signals (referrer/permissions policy) are reported but excluded from the actionable FP denominator.
